GENERATED-FILE CONFLICTS · #4049

Two PRs.
One Lab.
Zero conflicts.

Every playground PR used to edit one shared lab-manifest.json and one whole-file lab-data.ts. Five rebases in one lane on 2026-09-10 conflicted on nothing else. Pick two PRs below and watch the three-way merge under each layout. The base already holds the entries shown in grey.

Old: one file, prepend at line 1



Aggregate sorted by date


Fragments + slug-sorted aggregate









Why the count lies


Resolve the old file with --theirs and you keep B's entry and drop A's. The base had 6, main has 7, the branch has 7: a reviewer checking "did it go up by one" sees exactly what they expect. The only honest check is by set: every fragment in the aggregate, nothing in the aggregate without a fragment. That check now runs in CI on every PR head (node docs/site/scripts/lab-manifest.mjs --check), after a fresh rebuild that fails on any byte of drift.



What changed


The source of truth is one file per entry, docs/site/lab-manifest/<slug>.json, owned by one PR. The aggregate is generated sorted by slug, one entry per line, so two additions land on two different lines. Newest-first ordering moved into the gallery component: sorting the file by date would drop every same-day addition into the same gap. Two slugs adjacent in the alphabet can still touch on the aggregate, and the rule for that is the last control above: take either side, run npm run build, commit. Never hand-resolve a generated file.


Fragments live under docs/site/, not next to the page, because prune-playgrounds archives docs/<branch>/ off main after 30 days and the Lab entry must outlive the directory.
